patronOf.en-US: Abbess of Kildare, Patroness of Ireland
patronOf.pt-BR: Abadessa de Kildare, Padroeira da Irlanda

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Outward resemblance to Our Lady was St. Bridgid's peculiar privilege; but all are bound to grow like her in interior purity of heart.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A semelhança exterior com Nossa Senhora foi o privilégio peculiar de Santa Brígida; mas todos estão obrigados a crescer como ela na pureza interior do coração.

meta.face: An Irishwoman of about forty-five with a fair, freckled, fresh complexion and a WIDE, OBLONG face — broad, flat cheekbones and a LONG, firm, rounded jaw; a straight nose, a little long, with a rounded tip; large, wide-set, clear blue eyes under straight, copper-brown brows; a wide, calm mouth; a few strands of copper-red hair at the brow under the white veil; a steady, warm gaze toward us.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book gives her white habit and cloak and the lamp-and-fire tradition of Kildare; Wikipedia's iconography section gives the rush cross, the crozier, the lamp and the cow, and the Harry Clarke-school window at Cong (lead image) shows her veiled in white with a lamp. The book calls her outward resemblance to Our Lady her privilege; we do not borrow Our Lady's face from `recurring-figures.md`, so that she is not mistaken for her. The freckled, oblong face is our choice, kept apart from `bridget_sweden`.
